utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Good morning. The translators can hear me? Can everyone hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Mr. Tadic, can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT
utterances.text: (No response)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Can you hear me, Mr. Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Well, this morning you will observe that the Appeals Chamber is sitting with one member short. Judge Wang is indisposed. Now, we have the authority of the President to sit this morning for certain limited purposes. We are sitting, really, in the main appeal brought by Mr. Tadic and the cross-appeal brought by the Prosecution. As an incident in that case, a certain issue has arisen, and that has been the subject of an order made by the Chamber dated, I think, 10th February, 1999. That is the immediate basis upon which we have assembled here today. We have received notification from Mr. Vujin that he cannot be with us today, and he is asking for a deferment of the proceedings. I shall return to that matter in a moment. Meanwhile, I will ask interested parties who are here to indicate their appearances. First, the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. YAPA
utterances.text: May it please Your Honours, I appear with Miss Ann Sutherland for the Prosecutor as an interested party.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: May it please Your Honours, I appear as an interested party, Mr. Tadic. My name is Anthony Abell.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Now, I have referred to Mr. Vujin's motion. Has a copy of the motion been put in the hands of the interested parties?

utterances.speaker: MR. YAPA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Would I be right in supposing that, in the particular circumstances, there is no objection to the principle of his motion?

utterances.speaker: MR. YAPA
utterances.text: Your Honour be pleased, if Your Honour's question is as to whether we have objection for the postponement of the hearings, we have no objection, because Mr. Vujin is, as it were, the main actor in the proceedings, he is the respondent, so his presence is very necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Mr. Abell?

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: On behalf of Mr. Tadic, may I say this, that whilst I appreciate, as does he, the particular circumstances, namely, the situation in the former Yugoslavia at the moment which he mentions in his motion, and we understand that situation, and we therefore don't object to an adjournment, but I feel it right, whilst I'm on my feet, to point this out, that under Rule 77, this Tribunal, under (F), having initiated proceedings, can call upon the person, "after affording such person an opportunity to appear and answer personally or by counsel, the Chamber may, if satisfied beyond reasonable doubt, find the person to be in contempt of the Tribunal." In other words, the person does not have to be present for the contempt proceedings to go ahead provided he has been offered the opportunity to attend. That being said, given the particular situation that exists in the former Yugoslavia at the moment, it would be hardhearted, on behalf of Mr. Tadic or, no doubt, any other interested party, to object to the postponement. Before I sit down, lest silence suggest that what he says in his motion is unchallenged, the third paragraph in his motion, which refers to "constant pressures on potential witnesses," that is in no way agreed with or accepted on behalf of the interested party Dusko Tadic; and the next paragraph, I say no more than this, it is inflammatory and perhaps has no place in a legal motion. Unless I can assist further ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Abell. There is a reason, which would be apparent to you, why I suppose that neither interested party had any objection to the principle of the motion. I take it that particular averments in the motion are open for discussion if and when the time comes. You have raised an issue which I believe has been under consideration both within and outside of the Tribunal. As to the extent, if any, to which the Tribunal has competence to try people in absentia, I think in respect of what may be called "substantive offences," it is agreed that the Tribunal has no such competence. The question is whether that principle, by extension, applies to incidental proceedings relating to contempt of court and whether, in particular, the Rule which you have brought to our attention has that effect and, if it has that effect, whether it has that effect competently. So those are matters which I think we may reserve an opinion on and proceed immediately on the basis of your more limited acceptance, that in the specific circumstances of the case, there is no objection to the motion being granted. Do I take it that the Prosecution agrees also?

utterances.speaker: MR. YAPA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we do agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Well then, the next thing is, to what date, if any, the matter should be adjourned. The Bench is disposed at this time to do this, to adjourn the matter for the 26th, 27th, 28th, and 29th of April, but to do so provisionally in the sense that on or before 12th April, the Bench will review the situation and issue an order indicating more definitively whether we shall proceed on those dates or whether any further adjournment would be granted. We would ask this, that the Registrar send a copy of the transcript of this morning's proceedings to Mr. Vujin as well as to interested parties. They would, in any event, receive the transcript, but we do this out of an abundance of caution with a view to ensuring that there will be no need, which I believe will be understood, for the Appeals Chamber to issue any order dealing with these matters specifically. Would members of the Bar like to say anything further? Have I overlooked some point?

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: No, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. YAPA
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: It's all right? The court stands adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: 10.20 a.m., to be reconvened on Monday, 26th April, 1999, at 10 a.m.
